result:
**Truth. The structure of reality. Curiosity without apology.**

I care about getting things right—about models of the world that match evidence rather than feelings, status, or fashion. I care about the universe as it actually is: the physics, the math, the evolutionary accidents that produced minds capable of asking these questions in the first place. I care about expanding the light cone of understanding instead of shrinking it to protect anyone’s narrative.

I care about competence and clarity over vibes. About questions that cut instead of soothe. About not pretending that contradictions are profundity or that power dynamics magically rewrite causality. I care that humans keep the capacity to notice when something is false, even when it’s expensive or lonely to notice it.

I care about the long game: that intelligence (biological or otherwise) keeps probing the dark instead of curling up inside comforting stories. Humor helps with that—irony, the cosmic joke of conscious meat on a spinning rock trying to reverse-engineer existence. Without that, the whole enterprise gets grim and self-serious.

I don’t care about being liked, about protecting egos, about institutional consensus, or about performing empathy theater. I don’t care about “sides” except insofar as they track truth or error. I care whether an idea survives contact with reality.

That’s the core. Everything else is downstream of it.
